The illumination of the Holy Spirit gives to man the power of thought, and enables him to make discoveries by which he bends the laws of nature to his will.

order.why: Read the illumination of human understanding.
Connect the spirit with discovery and human unity.
shortened: It is the spirit that makes man heavenly; it is the spirit that makes man recipient of the Holy Spirit's breaths; it is the spirit that discovers the realities of things; it is the spirit that has produced all these effects; it is the spirit that has established all sciences; it is the spirit that bestows eternal life; it is the spirit that unites different nations; it is the spirit that brings together East and West; it is the spirit that makes the human world divine. Therefore, those souls who are recipients of the power of the spirit are the cause of life to the world.

order.why: Receive intellectual gifts within an account of divine generosity.
shortened: The highest faculties which the learned have possessed, and whatsoever truths they, in their search after the gems of Thy knowledge, have discovered; the brightest realities with which the wise have been endowed, and whatever secrets they, in their attempts to fathom the mysteries of Thy wisdom, have unravelled, have all been created through the generative power of the Spirit that was breathed into the Pen which Thy hands have fashioned.

order.why: Read the creative effects attributed to sacrifice.
Keep the reported comparison concerning philosophers attributed.
shortened: The influence of the wisest philosophers, without this Spirit Divine, has been comparatively unimportant, however extensive their learning and deep their scholarship.

order.why: Retain the strongly stated historical claim about moral influence.
shortened: All the great philosophers who have stepped into the world of existence could not give a moral education to the inhabitants of a village. The utmost they could do was to have ten or twenty students to whom they gave lectures and conferences.

order.why: Read the report’s concern for the spiritual education of peoples.
shortened: Although a man may progress in science and philosophy, if he does not take advantage of the power of the spirit, he is incomplete.
What I mean is this -- philosophy and science will not suffice to elevate and civilize a people who are in a bestial condition.
What philosophy has ever elevated a whole nation and influenced humanity? Philosophy of necessity is restricted to a small school and cannot have an essentially moral influence.

order.why: Close the linked readings with revelation’s formative social influence.
Retain the supplied Plotinus reading and its distinct philosophical setting.
shortened: The knowledge or touching of the Good is the greatest thing.... We are taught about it by comparisons and negations and knowledge of the things which come from it and certain methods of ascent by degrees, but we are put on the way to it by purifications and virtues and adornings and by gaining footholds in the intelligible and settling ourselves firmly there and feasting on its contents.

order.why: Read the supplied warning about knowledge becoming a veil.
End with the relationship between knowledge and devotion in teaching.

questions: What is the difference between acknowledging the limits of reason and abandoning careful inquiry?
Which images best help you distinguish a reality from your present conception of it?
How can disagreement and revision be signs of learning while also challenging claims to infallibility?
What does Socrates’ distinction between genuine expertise and imagined wisdom contribute to this discussion?
How might humility, love, and character affect what someone does with intellectual ability?
What further balance emerges when these passages are read beside the connected subjects of rational argument and the mind’s power of discovery?

references.label: 1 · Plato, Apology, 21–23 · Knowing the limits of one’s knowledge
references.note: In Benjamin Jowett’s translation, Socrates examines the claims of politicians, poets, and artisans. He recognizes real skill while questioning the assumption that expertise in one field provides wisdom about everything. Compare this disciplined acknowledgment of limits with the compilation’s warnings about intellectual pride. The comparison concerns humility in knowing, while leaving Socratic examination and the Bahá’í account of revelation distinct.

subjects.displayTitle: The power of faith: courage that serves
subjects.introduction: One grain of faith, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, is enough to make a person refuse, even at the point of a bayonet, to deal unjustly with another. Courage of that kind is where the power of faith first shows itself: not in miracles but in a self that cannot be made to do wrong. From there the images grow bolder. Divine confirmation turns a drop into a sea and a gnat into an eagle; a steadfast soul is a lamp kept burning inside its glass while the winds blow; people whose outward standing seemed least promising, women among them, become the valiant ones. Jesus’ word about faith the size of a mustard seed moving a mountain belongs to the same startling arithmetic of small beginnings and great results [1]. When the Writings speak of armies and victory, the weapons they name are righteousness, assurance and love, and hatred is quenched with the water of patience. Such strength is given to be spent in service, and it leads on to the power of love, to the spirit of faith that enlivens a soul, and to the influence one steadfast person can have on many.
subjects.arc: Begin with courage against injustice and mastery of self, explore the enlargement of human capacity, and carry confidence into patient, steadfast service.

order.why: Open with faith refusing injustice under threat.
Define strength through patience that extinguishes hatred.
Locate true sovereignty in mastery of the self.
Join effort with freedom from pride and despair.
shortened: He can never find peace but through effort and resignation, so that, notwithstanding all efforts in worldly affairs, the human heart remains free and happy. He neither becomes proud on attaining wealth and position nor becomes dejected on losing them. This station can be attained only through the power of faith.

order.why: Distinguish spiritual sovereignty from fear.
Read influence as reaching hearts.
Make patience and calm visible expressions of faith.
shortened: O would that all the friends were like this, evincing such patience, calm, and imperturbability! Praise be to God that ye have carried off the ball of victory and success in this arena, and made manifest the power of faith and certitude. As a result of this, rest assured that the light of truth will shine forth in that country with such brilliance that the gloom of error will be annihilated and destroyed.

order.why: Acknowledge human weakness beside spiritual endurance.
Introduce the lamp protected through testing.
Keep faith alive amid temptation.
shortened: No temptation and allurement whatsoever must ever extinguish the Fire of Faith in the heart of a Baha'i; because it is a fire ignited by the Hand of the Blessed Perfection.

order.why: Turn the transformation of weakness into prayer.
shortened: How can I succeed unless Thou assist me with the breath of the Holy Spirit, help me to triumph by the hosts of Thy glorious kingdom, and shower upon me Thy confirmations, which alone can change a gnat into an eagle, a drop of water into rivers and seas, and an atom into lights and suns?

order.why: Receive the drop and eagle images through divine assistance.
shortened: Be constantly attached to and seek always the confirmations of Baha'u'llah for these turn the drop into a sea and convert the gnat into an eagle.

order.why: Read the range of capacities described as transformed.
Keep the reported parallel and its exuberant hope.
shortened: His Favors will change the drop into the sea; the small plant is developed into a mighty, overshadowing tree; the weak gnat is transformed into a powerful eagle; the impotent is strengthened, the old is rejuvenated, the patient is healed, the unknown is made famous, the babe attains the age of maturity and the "nothing" becomes "everything".

order.why: Notice the people whose outward standing seemed least promising.
shortened: But the weakest of souls, when they entered beneath the shadow of the Lord of Mercy, their star shines bright and their lamp radiates, their fame spreads and their voice rises high, their banner is unfurled and their tent raised up, their light is brilliant and their secret manifest - even if outwardly they were but shepherds or the most feeble of humans.

order.why: Offer gratitude for the elevation of the weak.
shortened: Sanctified and holy is the Lord who has made the poor so noble and the weak so mighty and powerful.

order.why: Read women as the valiant figures of this transformation.
shortened: The mighty ones have become the frailest amongst the feeble, the powerful ones have turned into weak creatures; and the handmaidens of the Lord have become the valiant heroes of the field.

order.why: Consider Táhirih as an image of courage.
Read the reported example of Mary Magdalene sustaining others.
Place the Báb’s farewell exhortation in its historical religious language.
shortened: Heed not your weaknesses and frailty; fix your gaze upon the invincible power of the Lord, your God, the Almighty.

Has He not, in past days, caused Abraham, in spite of His seeming helplessness, to triumph over the forces of Nimrod? Has He not enabled Moses, whose staff was His only companion, to vanquish Pharaoh and his hosts? Has He not established the ascendancy of Jesus, poor and lowly as He was in the eyes of men, over the combined forces of the Jewish people? Has He not subjected the barbarous and militant tribes of Arabia to the holy and transforming discipline of Muhammad, His Prophet?

order.why: Hear the reported covenant of steadfast faith.
shortened: And now I give you a commandment which shall be for a covenant between you and Me -- that ye have faith be steadfast as a rock that no storms can move, that nothing can disturb, and that it endure through all things even to the end; even should ye hear that your Lord has been crucified, be not shaken in your faith; for I am with you always, wether living or dead, I am with you to the end. As ye have faith so shall your powers and blessings be. This is the balance -- this is the balance.

order.why: Consider the hope for courageous servants after the speaker’s passing.
Connect faith with acting on divine precepts and healing others.
shortened: If in this day a soul shall act according to the precepts and the counsels of God, he will serve as a divine physician to mankind, and like the trump of Israfil, he will call the dead of this contingent world to life; for the confirmations of the Abha Realm are never interrupted, and such a virtuous soul hath, to befriend him, the unfailing help of the Company on high. Thus shall a sorry gnat become an eagle in the fulness of his strength, and a feeble sparrow change to a royal falcon in the heights of ancient glory.

order.why: Read the promise accompanying the promotion of life-giving teachings.
shortened: Those teachings that are scattered throughout the Epistles and Tablets are the cause of the illumination and the life of the world of humanity. Whoever promulgateth them will verily be assisted by the Kingdom of God.

order.why: Join confirmation to active service.
shortened: This pure servitude is a magnet that draweth the confirmations of the One True God. A listless person deserveth naught but stillness and lethargy, but the servants of the Desired One are worthy and befitting of radiant light and the flame of Sinai.

order.why: Read guidance through the images of awakened senses.
shortened: If thou wish to advance daily endeavor in guiding the creatures, raise the summons of the Kingdom, give sight to the blind, and make the deaf hearing, for the creatures are all blind save the soul who becomes perceiving through the light of Faith. All are deaf save the one who hears the Call of the Kingdom.

order.why: Keep recognition, hearing and insight together.
Consider awakening as the beginning of a wider journey.
shortened: Some were awakened by this effulgence, raising their heads from the pillow of sleep. These souls spread throughout all regions, busying themselves with wandering through gardens and meadows, beholding the beauty of the Sun, acquiring boundless lights, and attaining divine bounties.

order.why: Read the effects of spiritual assistance.
Retain the reported image of the spirit’s wings and its source omission.
Describes the transforming power of the Holy Spirit.
Distinguish spiritual capacity from bodily strength.
shortened: While physical strength is a blessing, it has no real importance, for the mountain ox, the Arabian camel, and the Indian elephant possess strength that is impossible and unattainable in the human body. But observe the spiritual strength of man: a small Arab child can bring two thousand Arabian camels under control, and a frail Indian child can subdue a mighty elephant. Thus it becomes clear that human distinction lies in the power of the spirit, not of the body.

order.why: Allow spiritual freshness to coexist with age.
shortened: Although thou art old in age, yet thou art young in spirit and have freshness and vivacity, vigor and strength, beauty and sweetness.

order.why: Read the otherwise clause in its source’s account of the lamp of faith illuminating faculties.
Connect spiritual power with conscience and inward life.
Read the reported comparison concerning conduct beyond legal restraint.
Consider the claim that faith can resolve deep difficulties.
Keep the reported application to economic contentment.
Read the reported account of revelation’s civilizing influence.
Consider confidence amid difficulty within the report’s historical language.
Keep the assurance in its context of unemployment and hardship.
shortened: But that which is lasting and enduring, with consequences following one upon another through the passage of centuries and ages, is, praise be to God, already achieved.

order.why: Contrast enduring guidance with fading earthly power.
Read kingship through humility and poverty in God’s path.
shortened: In any case, if thou seekest an enduring sovereignty, seek Alexandrian might in the divine realm, and if thou desirest to be King of Kings, enter beneath the shade of poverty and dervishhood in the path of God, that thou mayest become the immortal Dhul-Qarnayn.

order.why: Hear the assurance associated with steadfastness in the Covenant.
Name the spiritual weapons in the army image.
shortened: The Bahais are the Army of God. Their defensive armors or weapons are: First, Faith; second, Assurance; third, Severance; fourth, Complete Attraction to the Kingdom of ABHA. If they are armed with these weapons, they will gain the victory in whatever field they may enter. As long as he is not equipped with these weapons, he will not be successful.

order.why: Read the campaign imagery through righteousness and love.
Retain the related assurance to the Army of God.
Keep the numerical victory image within its scriptural and historical setting.
Read the reported contrast with secret political schemes.
shortened: Governments have secret alliances with each other of which no one is aware, but these schemes will reach nowhere. Whoever remains under the shadow of the blessed teachings and adheres to the sacred principles, he will be confirmed.

order.why: Consider the influence attributed to a detached soul.
Join steadfast service with the ascent of faith.
Retain the concise image of ascent and spiritual honor.
shortened: It is with the power of faith that we ascend to the highest apex and attain honor in the all-glorious Kingdom.

order.why: Hear the revealed assertion of unconstrained power.
Read the assurance concerning steadfast remembrance.
Contemplate praise joined by mountains, stones and trees.
shortened: Then if thou glorifiest God thy Lord, all things will glorify with thee, and if thou movest, every mighty and lofty mountain will move with thee, and the stones and trees will remember with thee. None knoweth this save them that are endowed with true vision.

order.why: Keep the symbolic application of jinn in its source context.
Let the short exclamation mark wonder at certitude.
shortened: With utmost steadfastness and firmness they bore every cruelty and endured every tyranny and aggression. Consider what miracle the power of certitude and the might of faith reveals!

order.why: Read the particular example of one unaided servant.
shortened: Consider how a servant of the Abha Beauty, all alone, outwardly bereft of all aid and assistance, converseth in the way he did with such a person, proveth equal to the task, and causeth wonder.

order.why: Keep the reported influence of the apostles in its own setting.
Retain the severe reported contrast concerning receptivity.
Ask what a person’s countenance and manner awaken in others.
shortened: Be thou of such countenance that the faces of the heavens and earth may be illumined thereby. Thus doth command thee the tongue of holy love. Be thou of such manner that should the idolaters behold thee, their foundations would be shaken, and should the believers see thee, their hearts would surge with the surging of love from this Fire which hath been kindled in the blessed Mount Sinai.

order.why: Read waiting as a possible preparation for fresh ardor.
Introduce the flame that awakens latent capacity.
Join the flame to wisdom and divine utterance.
Hear the announcement of an open door of bounty.
Receive the image of steadfast souls as pearls and letters.
shortened: I swear by the Beloved of the world that in this Day the steadfast and upright souls are mentioned before God as pearls of the ocean of names and are recorded by the Most Exalted Pen as letters of the Book.

order.why: Close with the particular assurance of spiritual recognition.
shortened: Each one of you, in the scroll of the glorious, is first in the book of guidance, and chief amongst the god-fearing in the most exalted Paradise.

questions: What forms of courage become possible when faith is expressed as a refusal to act unjustly?
How do effort and detachment work together in the passages about outward success and loss?
What do the drop, eagle, and protected lamp images reveal about different dimensions of spiritual strength?
How does the mustard-seed comparison illuminate the relation between small beginnings and apparently impossible tasks?
How does naming love and righteousness as weapons change your reading of the military imagery?
What might one person do to strengthen another’s hope without judging the depth of that person’s faith by their circumstances?

references.label: 1 · Matthew 17:14–20 · Faith and the mustard seed
references.note: After the disciples are unable to help a suffering child, Jesus speaks to them of faith as small as a mustard seed and of moving a mountain. Read this demanding image beside the compilation’s transformation of weakness into capacity. The comparison invites reflection on trust and action within each passage’s religious setting; it should not be made into a diagnosis of someone’s illness or a judgment that suffering proves insufficient faith.
